questions.query: Are the sixteen Batch Lab tiles real isolated native construction attempts?
facts: Each active attempt uses the existing worker and its own native World; padding is not the isolation boundary.
The static M0–M2 material prototype preserves material identities and does not advance dynamic physics.
Queued operations require native completion receipts before being counted as applied.

questions.query: Do Batch Lab P0 through P3 prove which model or prompt builds better architecture?
facts: Matched deterministic controls demonstrate construction and measurement, not model or prompt quality.
P2/P3 deliver source-grounded text cards; all variants share the same supported tool capabilities.
Real model comparisons, held-out quality gains and human preferences require separately executed evidence.

questions.query: How do I run the Windows Batch Lab evaluator, stop it and retain reproducible results?
facts: Extract the complete source-matched evaluator, verify the checksum and launch Open Workbench.cmd.
Open optional Batch Lab, run 2x2 or4x4 examples, inspect and compare actual native results, Stop then wait for receipts.
Save/Open retains attempts; Replay uses source/program without inference; physical Windows11/NVIDIA acceptance is separate.
